summary: Redwood demo focused on Eval/Quality Monitoring: building prompt sets, configuring regression alerts, running A/B comparisons, and integrating with Emerald Health's evaluation workflow. Customer interested in private deployment constraints (PHI), RBAC, audit logs, and runbook for POC benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Lindsay Carter, Ravi Patel, Sofia Gomez (Emerald Health)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex, i'll run the quick intro. priya from our se team is here to do the walkthrough. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lindsay: good, thanks. excited to see the eval stuff - we've been trying to consolidate our prompt sets and keep track of regressions after model bumps.
[00:15] Priya: great. quick agenda - show Redwood Optimize eval monitor, prompt set management in the console, regression alerting, and an A/B comparison demo using your sample prompts. we'll also cover integrations (okta, kms) and private options for PHI data.
[00:28] Ravi: quick thing - our infra is in a VPC, we need VPC peering or private link and KMS with customer-managed keys, ok?
[00:34] Priya: totally. Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and VPC peering; we'll show the network diagram later. for now i'll share the console - link: https://console.redwood.ai/demo-tenant (note: demo tenant with sample evals).
[00:45] Priya: so here's the Eval dashboard - prompt sets are first-class. you can group prompts by intent, add expected outputs, tags, and automated scoring metrics.
[00:55] [screen share noise / minor transcript artefact]
[01:05] Priya: i'll create a new prompt set called "clinical-summary-checks" - add prompts, expected gold output, and then choose metrics. common ones: BLEU/ROUGE for summaries, embedding cosine for semantic similarity, and a custom script metric for business rules.
[01:20] Sofia: how do we handle stochastic outputs? some of our prompts are generation-based and have multiple acceptable answers.
[01:26] Priya: good question. you can add multiple accepted answers and weight them; we also support embedding-based similarity thresholds so you can accept paraphrases. the UI shows distribution of scores across model runs.
[01:40] Alex: and for your CI, you can run these prompt sets programmatically via the Redwood API - call /evals/run with a prompt_set_id and model_version, returns per-prompt metrics and artifacts (outputs, embeddings, scores).
[01:55] Lindsay: does it capture inputs and outputs for audit? we need traceability for PHI handling and compliance.
[02:02] Priya: yes - audit logs and per-token traces are in the Private plan; logs can be routed to your SIEM and we support retention policies. note the transcript may say "SOC two" sometimes, but the doc is SOC 2 Type II.
[02:15] Ravi: okay. what about regression alerts - we want to get notified when quality drops after a model update.
[02:21] Priya: alerts are driven off your baseline. choose a baseline model run and set thresholds per-metric. e.g., average embedding cosine must stay above 0.85, rouge-l no lower than 0.72. when the delta exceeds the threshold, Redwood sends alert channels: slack, pagerduty, email, webhook. you can configure per-team routing.
[02:40] [00:00 speaker cross-talk; minor hiccup]
[02:48] Priya: i'll simulate a regression - run model v1.2 baseline, then run v1.3 and show the A/B comparison report.
[02:55] [30s wait as demo runs]
[03:25] Priya: ok results done. the A/B compare shows per-prompt diffs, aggregated metrics, and a waterfall highlighting which prompts drove the overall drop. you can click into any prompt to see examples where the newer model hallucinated or changed formatting.
[03:40] Sofia: can we tie this to our PR workflow? like block a deploy if regression is above a threshold?
[03:46] Alex: yep - Redwood has a gating API. you can call /evals/compare in your CI and fail the job based on returned status. we also integrate with GitHub Checks to surface the report.
[03:58] Lindsay: for the scoring scripts - our clinicians have heuristics (like preserve med names and dosages). can we plug those in?
[04:05] Priya: absolutely. you can upload custom scoring scripts (python) that run server-side in a sandbox; they return a numeric score per prompt. we show script logs and allow test runs.
[04:18] Ravi: security - encryption at rest and in transit? where are model weights stored for private deployments?
[04:24] Priya: at-rest encryption uses your KMS (customer-managed) for Private; hosted model variants keep weights in our managed infra, but for Private we can host weights in your environment or a private air-gapped option. we provide an audit runbook.
[04:38] [transcription noise: "K V cash" appears once]
[04:45] Alex: talking about cost - Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and batching configs per-model to reduce token cost while keeping your eval metrics within tolerance. this ties into the per-route dashboards.
[04:58] Priya: demo time - here's an A/B report exported as CSV and a visual diff. note the per-prompt tags: "critical", "formatting", "clinical-safety" - you can weight them so regressions on critical prompts trigger immediate alerts.
[05:12] Sofia: how many prompt sets and prompts can we manage? we have thousands of prompts across products.
[05:18] Priya: platform scales - we've customers with tens of thousands of prompts. you can bulk upload via CSV or call the API. there's also a prompt de-duplication view and similarity clustering to help consolidate.
[05:30] Lindsay: ok show me a real alert flow.
[05:34] Priya: sure - i have a pre-seeded alert. triggering now... alert fires to slack (we show the slack message), it links back to the A/B report and the specific failing prompts.
[05:45] [pause]
[05:50] Ravi: do alerts include sample outputs with redactions? we can't share PHI to external services.
[05:55] Priya: Redwood can redact PII via configurable patterns before routing; with Private you can keep raw outputs on-prem and only surface hashed artifacts or embeddings to hosted dashboards.
[06:10] Alex: quick note on integrations - we support Okta SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles per-team, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog).
[06:24] Lindsay: what about sample rates for monitoring? we don't want to send everything off-host.
[06:29] Priya: you set sampling policies - e.g., sample 100% of production requests for critical routes, 5% for low-risk. sampling + KV caching reduces noise and cost.
[06:40] Sofia: can we store gold outputs in our S3 or in the Redwood store?
[06:44] Priya: both options. gold sets can be stored in your S3 (preferred for PHI) and Redwood will pull them for eval runs, or stored in Redwood with controlled retention.
[06:56] [10 min mark, demo continues with deeper dive into API calls]
[07:10] Priya: here's an API example: POST /evals/run {"prompt_set":"clinical-summary-checks","model":"redwood-qa-2.0"} returns run_id. then GET /evals/report/{run_id}. the report contains per-prompt scores, example outputs, and diffs for A/B.
[07:30] Ravi: what's the latency for eval runs? if we run 1k prompts how long?
[07:35] Priya: depends on model and hosting. for hosted batch evals we parallelize and typically complete 1k small prompts in minutes for smaller models; for long-gen models it's longer. for Dedicated you can reserve capacity to hit SLA.
[07:50] Sofia: can we schedule recurring runs? like nightly regression suites?
[07:53] Priya: yes - schedule runs or trigger from CI. you can also configure auto-baseline refreshes on major model upgrades.
[08:05] Alex: i'll talk about pricing briefly - eval runs are metered (per prompt / per compute bucket). we'll share a sample pricing sheet.
[08:12] Lindsay: we have procurement questions but will surface after security review. primary blocker is PHI handling and a SOC2 + BA agreement.
[08:20] Priya: we have a SOC 2 Type II report and a standard BA (business associate) template for healthcare customers; i'll include in the follow-up packet.
[08:28] [demo wrap-up visuals]
[08:34] Priya: quick recap: prompt sets, custom metrics/scripts, baselines, A/B compare, regression alerts, integrations (SSO/KMS/SIEM), and Private options for PHI.
[08:45] Lindsay: this looks promising. couple of asks: 1) show an end-to-end POC run with our real prompts, 2) run a baseline with our current model and one candidate open model, 3) show deployment gating integration into our CI.
[08:58] Alex: noted - action items in the next steps. we'll provision trial access and a POC eval runner.
[09:05] Ravi: one operational question - do you keep historical run artifacts indefinitely? we need 7 years for some records.
[09:11] Priya: retention is configurable, but long-term archival is usually S3 export or customer-managed retention; we can work with legal on retention policies for the BA.
[09:24] Sofia: just to flag - some prompts are sensitive and we'd prefer only embeddings be sent to your hosted service. is that doable?
[09:30] Priya: yes, you can configure redaction and only ship anonymized embeddings; for Private you can keep outputs local and push only metrics.
[09:38] [closing cadence]
[09:41] Alex: thanks all. i'll follow up with SOC2, pricing, and next meeting invite. priya will provision the trial and SE-run POC.
[09:50] Lindsay: thanks, talk soon.

End transcript.
